q: 1. A sphere in isometric projection appears as a circle of diameter
options: equal to the diameter of sphere
greater than the diameter of sphere
explain: In isometric projection (using the true isometric scale), a sphere projects as a circle whose diameter equals the sphere's actual diameter, since the same foreshortening ratio applies equally in every direction on a sphere.

q: 2. Projection of an object shown by three views is known as
explain: Multiview (orthographic) projection represents an object using multiple related views (typically front, top, and side) obtained by projecting perpendicularly onto mutually perpendicular planes.

q: 3. For orthographic projections, B.I.S. recommends the following
explain: The Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS/IS codes) recommends first angle projection as the standard method for orthographic drawings in India.

q: 4. Which of the following theories of mathematics is used by a CAD (Computer Aided Design) software in creating a perspective design?
explain: CAD perspective transformations rely on vector analysis to compute projections of 3D coordinates onto the picture plane.

q: 5. While making cavalier projections the ellipse is preferably drawn by .............
explain: In cavalier (and other oblique) projections, circular features on the receding faces are typically constructed using the oblong (rectangle-based) method to plot the true elliptical shape.

q: 6. In case of diametric projection
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: In dimetric projection two of the three axes make equal angles with the picture plane (are equally inclined), while the third differs.

q: 7. The angle between isometric axes is
explain: In isometric projection, the three principal axes are spaced equally at $120^{\circ}$ to each other.

q: 8. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is
explain: Due to the tilt of the object in isometric projection, all lines are foreshortened to approximately 81.5% of their true length.

q: 9. In first angle projection, the object comes .............
explain: First angle projection follows the sequence Observer → Object → Plane, so the object is positioned between the observer and the projection plane.

q: 10. Why perspective drawing is done by manufacturer?
options: It is easy to express in the market
explain: Its primary benefit for manufacturers is that it presents the product in a visually appealing, realistic manner.

q: 11. A point is 20 mm below HP and 30 mm behind VP. Its top view will be .............
explain: The top view of a point shows its distance behind VP; since the point is below HP, its top view is conventionally drawn above the XY line, at a distance equal to the distance behind VP, i.e., 30 mm above XY.

q: 12. If both the front and the top views of a point lie on the same side of the reference line the point may be situated in following angels .............
explain: When both views fall on the same side of the XY line, the point lies in either the second angle (above HP, behind VP) or the fourth angle (below HP, in front of VP), both of which yield views on the same side of the reference line.

q: 13. View of circle in orthographic is
explain: A circle appears as a circle if parallel to the plane, but as an ellipse or a line if inclined to the plane.

q: 14. In isometric projection, circles are represented as ellipse on
explain: Since all three isometric faces are inclined to the line of sight, circles on any face appear as ellipses.

q: 15. A 100 m long line making 30 degree with the vertical, show its projection on horizontal plane
explain: Projection on HP = $L \times \sin(\theta)$ if angle is with vertical. $100 \times \sin(30^{\circ}) = 100 \times 0.5 = 50\text{ m}$.

q: 16. If a thin set-square is kept perpendicular to both the horizontal and vertical planes, its true shape is seen in .............
explain: A plane perpendicular to both HP and VP is, by definition, parallel to the profile plane (PP), so its true shape appears in the side (profile) view.

q: 17. An isometric projection is pictorial drawing of
explain: Isometric projection is a pictorial representation that shows three faces (views) of an object in a single drawing.

q: 18. The isometric length of the edge of the cube is obtained by .............
explain: Note: per the answer key this option is marked correct; conventionally the isometric length is obtained by multiplying the true length by the isometric ratio (~0.816), which corresponds to option (c) rather than 'adding.'

q: 19. The section obtained when the section plane is inclined to the axis of cone and cuts all the generators on either side of the apex, is called ...........
explain: When the cutting plane is inclined to the axis and cuts all generators, the resulting conic section is an ellipse.

q: 20. First angle projection method and third angle projection method are used in .............
explain: First-angle and third-angle are the two internationally recognized conventions specifically for orthographic (multiview) projection, differing in the relative position of the object, plane, and observer.

q: 21. The solid which is generated by the revolution of a right angle triangle about one of its perpendicular sides which remains fixed is called .............
explain: Rotating a right-angled triangle around its altitude creates a cone.

q: 22. The purpose of sectional view is to show the
explain: Sectional views allow designers to show internal holes, cavities, and assembly details that are hidden from the outside.

q: 23. In case of diametric projection .............
options: two sides are not equally inclined
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'two sides are equal' is marked correct; in dimetric projection, two of the three principal axes are equally foreshortened (and hence scaled equally), which corresponds to option (d) in this reference's phrasing.

q: 24. Section lining is drawn with line at
explain: By convention, hatching/section lines are drawn at 45 degrees to the main outline of the sectioned part.

q: 25. One of the characteristics features of a perspective drawing is that objects are drawn:
options: smaller as their distance from the observer increases
larger as their distance from the observer increases
explain: Foreshortening and convergence in perspective mean that objects appear smaller as they move further away.

q: 26. The principal of oblique view drawing is to keep:
options: width and height axes at 90 degree
width, height and depth axes at 90 degree
explain: In Oblique projection, the front face (width and height) is kept parallel to the plane and at $90^{\circ}$ to each other, showing its true shape.

q: 27. Orthographic projection means .............
explain: 'Orthographic' derives from the Greek for 'right/straight writing,' referring to projection at a right angle (90°) — projectors perpendicular to the plane of projection.

q: 28. Which one is not engineerirg drawing?
explain: Cinema slides are artistic/entertainment media, not technical engineering drawings like building plans, road sections or machine elevations.

q: 29. In oblique projections, a semi circle parallel to the plane of projection appears as .............
explain: Any plane figure that is parallel to the plane of projection in oblique projection is not foreshortened and hence retains its true shape — so a semicircle parallel to the plane still appears as a semicircle.

q: 30. Presentation drawing are generally rendered due to
explain: Rendering in presentation drawings adds shadows, textures, and lighting to create a realistic effect for the viewer.

q: 31. The face of an object containing circles, irregular shapes, etc. is kept parallel to the plane of projection is known as .............
explain: In oblique projection, the face with circular or irregular details is deliberately kept parallel to the plane of projection so it can be drawn true to shape without distortion, while other faces recede at an angle.

q: 32. The base angles used for drawing an isometric projection are:
explain: Isometric drawing uses one vertical (0° from vertical) axis and two receding axes drawn at 30° to the horizontal.

q: 33. In the first angle method of orthographic projection
options: the object comes between the observer and the plane
the plane comes between the object and the observer
the observer comes between the object and the plane
explain: In first-angle projection, the sequence is Observer -> Object -> Plane.

q: 34. Most suitable hand drawn coloured perspective drawing paper is:
explain: Any good quality coloured paper is considered suitable for hand-drawn coloured perspective presentation drawings.

q: 35. When the receding lines are drawn to full size scale then the oblique projection is
explain: In Cavalier projection, the receding (depth) axis is drawn at its full actual length.

q: 36. A square in a regular multi-view projection appears in an isometric view as .............
explain: A square face, when drawn in isometric view (inclined to the viewer along isometric axes), is foreshortened into a rhombus shape.

q: 37. A square pyramid is resting on a face in the VP. The number of dotted lines that will appear in the front view .............
explain: With the square pyramid resting on a triangular face against VP, the hidden (invisible) edges behind the visible face project as two dotted (hidden) lines in the front view.

q: 38. The elevation is a:
explain: An elevation can refer to the front, back, or side view of an object depending on which vertical face is being projected.

q: 39. Methods for the development of solids are .............
explain: Note: per the answer key, 'triangular method' is marked as the sole correct answer, though in general practice, parallel-line, radial-line, and triangulation methods are all standard techniques for surface development of solids.

q: 40. Picture plane is
explain: The picture plane, on which the perspective image is formed, is taken as a vertical plane.

q: 41. Axonometric projection is a special type of .............
explain: Axonometric projection (including isometric, dimetric, trimetric) is a subtype of orthographic projection, using parallel projectors perpendicular to the plane but with the object rotated to show multiple faces.

q: 42. In the case of orthographic projection the number of view used are
explain: The complete orthographic (glass-box) system generally uses six principal views.

q: 43. Development of sphere is done by .............
options: parallel line or radial line method
explain: Since a sphere's doubly curved surface cannot be developed exactly, it is approximately developed using the zone (band) method or the lune (gore) method, both specialized techniques for spherical surfaces.

q: 44. In case of perspective projection, picture plane is placed .............
explain: In perspective projection, the picture plane is positioned between the observer's eye (station point) and the object, onto which the perspective view is projected.

q: 45. Isometric projection is .............
options: an orthographic projection of pictorial type
explain: Isometric projection is classified as a pictorial type of orthographic projection, since its parallel projectors remain perpendicular to the plane of projection while the object itself is tilted to reveal multiple faces.

q: 46. A circle in isometric projection appears as .............
explain: Because every face in isometric projection is inclined to the line of sight, a circle drawn on that face is foreshortened and appears as an ellipse.

q: 47. The distortion in oblique projections can be decreased by .............
options: placing the projection in correct scale
reducing the length of the receding lines
placing the projection obliquely to the plane of projection
enlarging the dimensions parallel to the plane of projection
explain: Reducing the length of the receding lines (as done in cabinet projection, using half scale) decreases the visual distortion/exaggeration that appears in oblique projections compared to full-scale cavalier projection.

q: 48. One plane projection is .............
explain: Both axonometric and oblique projections are examples of single (one) plane projection methods, where the entire 3D object is represented on one projection plane, unlike multiview (orthographic) projection which uses multiple planes.
